title: Caching + Batching Configuration: interactive presets, explainers, and guardrails for Console
creator: Liam Patel
description: Design an end-to-end UX surface in Redwood Console that exposes batching and caching configuration to customers via sensible presets, inline recommendations, and safety guardrails. The goal is to help engineers reduce per-token cost while preserving latency SLOs and avoiding surprising quality regressions. Deliverables: high-fidelity Figma screens, interactive prototype, copy for explainers/tooltips, accessibility checks, and handoff-ready specs for ENG and PM.
background: Customers repeatedly ask for guidance on how to tune batching and KV/prefix caching without risking latency regressions or model quality issues. Currently these knobs exist in the Dedicated/private config YAML but are opaque: defaults are conservative and support gets frequent tickets about "why latency spiked" after naive batching changes. This work is part of the Console: Cost & Performance Controls initiative to make performance levers discoverable and safe.

decisions: Expose batching and caching only via controlled presets + an advanced panel. Default to 'Balanced' for new accounts.
Provide an interactive cost/latency preview that estimates impact using sampled telemetry for the customer's own workloads (requires ENG-2201).
Add hard guardrails on max batch size and aggregate KV memory per model by tier; present 'risk level' badge if a user attempts to exceed those limits.
Offer built-in rollback and canary rollout recipe next to 'Apply' button to reduce blast radius.
Show inline explainers: short one-liners + expandable 'how this affects quality' section authored with Applied ML.
Do not allow automated aggressive caching presets for models marked as 'non-deterministic' until model-safety checks pass (flagged for Research follow-up).
